a: The CPU executes instructions: fetch, decode, execute.
RAM is fast volatile memory for running programs and data.
ROM is read-only (or rarely written) memory often used for firmware.
CPU cache is small fast memory that stores frequently used data/instructions.
A process is a running instance of a program with its own address space.
A thread is a unit of execution within a process that shares memory with other threads.
Deadlock is when processes wait forever for each other's resources.
A mutex is a lock that allows only one thread to enter a critical section.
A semaphore is a counter used to control access to a limited resource.
Virtual memory maps process address spaces to physical RAM and disk (swap).
A context switch saves one process/thread state and loads another so the CPU can multitask.
The kernel is the core of the OS managing hardware, processes, memory, and drivers.
A system call is how user programs request services from the kernel.
Endianness is byte order in memory: little-endian stores least significant byte first.
An ISA (instruction set architecture) defines the machine instructions a CPU understands.
Pipelining overlaps stages of instruction execution to improve throughput.
